claims.text: Periodic Bloom-filter updates burden communication-constrained systems.
claims.poster_quote: Periodic Bloom-filter updates burden communication-constrained systems.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Periodic Bloom-filter transmission can impose substantial overhead in communication-constrained distributed systems.
claims.reason: Section Abstract. The paper states that periodic transmission can impose substantial overhead in communication-constrained systems.

claims.text: The proposed method selects among OR-folded views that meet a maximum FPR, keeping the canonical filter unchanged.
claims.poster_quote: We select among OR-folded views that meet a maximum FPR, keeping the canonical filter unchanged.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The sender retains an unchanged canonical filter, constructs a catalog satisfying a maximum FPR, and selects the FPR-qualified representation with the largest retained length supported by the communication resources available at each reporting opportunity.
claims.reason: Section Abstract. The proposed method selects among FPR-qualified representations while keeping the canonical filter unchanged.

claims.text: Across two phishing URL datasets and three channel models, the proposed method improves efficiency and receiver freshness.
claims.poster_quote: Across two phishing URL datasets and three channel models, this improves efficiency and receiver freshness.
claims.label: unsupported
claims.reason: Section VII (Conclusion) states that adaptive folding improved communication efficiency and receiver freshness under the Five-State and Rayleigh models, but under the Gilbert-Elliott model it remained competitive in efficiency (not improved).

claims.text: Selection is driven by time-varying communication conditions rather than cardinality, and gains are largest when communication opportunities vary substantially.
claims.poster_quote: Selection is driven by time-varying communication conditions rather than cardinality, and gains are largest when communication opportunities vary substantially.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Unlike folding driven principally by cardinality and false-positive constraints, selection is driven by time-varying communication conditions.
claims.reason: Section Abstract. The paper states that selection is driven by time-varying communication conditions rather than cardinality, and that folding improves performance when communication opportunities vary substantially.

claims.text: The sender caches a catalog of representations, excluding any above the application-defined maximum FPR.
claims.poster_quote: The sender caches a catalog of representations, excluding any above the application-defined maximum FPR.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Each sender retains a complete canonical Bloom filter and generates or caches a catalog of representations at the retained-length ratios supported by the system. ... and representations exceeding the application-defined maximum FPR are excluded.
claims.reason: Section III.E. The sender caches a catalog of representations and excludes those exceeding the maximum FPR.

claims.text: At each reporting opportunity, the sender sends the largest qualified view that fits capacity, or defers the update.
claims.poster_quote: At each reporting opportunity it sends the largest qualified view that fits capacity, or defers the update.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: For a capacity-limited channel, this is the representation with the largest retained length whose total transmitted size, including the Bloom-filter payload and packet headers, fits within the available capacity. ... If no qualified representation can be delivered, the update is deferred.
claims.reason: Section III.E. The sender selects the largest representation that fits the capacity, or defers the update.

claims.text: Each report carries its retained length and a timestamp.
claims.poster_quote: Each report carries its retained length and a timestamp;
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Each transmitted update contains the selected Bloom-filter representation, its retained length m′, and a timestamp that serves as its report version.
claims.reason: Section III.E. Each update carries its retained length and a timestamp.

claims.text: The receiver installs only newer, completely delivered views without reconstructing the canonical filter.
claims.poster_quote: the receiver installs only newer, completely delivered views without reconstructing the canonical filter.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The receiver installs only a completely delivered update newer than its currently stored view and queries it using the coordinate mapping in Equation (5). ... Reconstruction of the canonical filter is neither required nor attempted
claims.reason: Section III.E. The receiver installs only newer, completely delivered updates without attempting reconstruction.

claims.text: Measured FPR rises smoothly as the filter is shrunk, so folding exposes many queryable sizes where compression gives one recoverable payload.
claims.poster_quote: Measured FPR rises smoothly as the filter is shrunk, so folding exposes many queryable sizes where compression gives one recoverable payload.
claims.label: unsupported
claims.reason: Section V.A states that the false positive rate 'increases gradually under moderate folding and then rises more rapidly as the reduced representation approaches saturation', which does not support the claim that it 'rises smoothly'.

claims.text: Prior folding reacts to cardinality, whereas the proposed method reacts to the channel.
claims.poster_quote: Prior folding reacts to cardinality; we react to the channel
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Sailhan and Stehr [7] select among integer-factor representations as cardinality changes to maintain a prescribed FPR range. ... In contrast, the present work holds the inserted set, canonical filter, and hash count fixed while treating current communication conditions as the online selection variable.
claims.reason: Section II. Prior folding reacts to cardinality, whereas the proposed method treats communication conditions as the online selection variable.

claims.text: Limitations of the study include fixed contents, simulated channels, and no fixed-fold baselines.
claims.poster_quote: Limits: fixed contents, simulated channels, and no fixed-fold baselines.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The controlled design uses two URL datasets at the same cardinality with fixed contents. This isolates channel-driven selection but does not establish generality across other workloads, cardinalities, occupancies, or changing contents. The simulated channel models provide repeatable capacity-variation, burst-loss, and fading conditions on paired traces, but are normalized to the complete sparse-filter wire size. ... Fixed folded representations are not included as baselines.
claims.reason: Section VI.C. The paper explicitly lists fixed contents, simulated channels, and the lack of fixed folded baselines as limitations.

claims.text: Bloom filters give compact membership with no false negatives.
claims.poster_quote: Bloom filters give compact membership with no false negatives
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Bloom filters (BFs) are compact probabilistic structures for approximate set membership, providing efficient insertion and queries with no false negatives and a controllable false-positive rate (FPR) [1].
claims.reason: Section I. Bloom filters provide approximate set membership with no false negatives.

claims.text: Complete-filter updates can be delayed or dropped, leaving stale receiver state.
claims.poster_quote: complete-filter updates can be delayed or dropped, leaving stale receiver state.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: When communication resources are constrained or time varying, complete-filter updates may be delayed or dropped, leaving stale receiver state.
claims.reason: Section I. Complete-filter updates may be delayed or dropped, leaving stale receiver state.

claims.text: Lossless compression preserves membership behavior yet yields a single payload.
claims.poster_quote: Lossless compression preserves membership behavior yet yields a single payload
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Lossless compressed BFs reduce transmission size without changing membership behavior [6], but produce a single payload determined by the filter contents.
claims.reason: Section I. Lossless compression reduces size without changing membership behavior but produces a single payload.

claims.text: Folding exposes smaller, directly queryable views.
claims.poster_quote: folding exposes smaller, directly queryable views.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: OR folding instead produces smaller, directly queryable views with increased FPR while preserving the no-false-negative property.
claims.reason: Section I. OR folding produces smaller, directly queryable views.

claims.text: The proposed method selects the transmitted view from external, time-varying channel conditions.
claims.poster_quote: We select the transmitted view from external, time-varying channel conditions.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: This paper addresses the complementary problem of selecting a transmitted folded view according to an external, time-varying communication constraint.
claims.reason: Section I. The proposed method selects a folded view according to external, time-varying communication constraints.

claims.text: The paper contributes an online selection policy for FPR-qualified folded views.
claims.poster_quote: An online selection policy for FPR-qualified folded views
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: an online policy for selecting an FPR-qualified OR-folded representation under time-varying communication constraints;
claims.reason: Section I. The first listed contribution is an online policy for selecting an FPR-qualified OR-folded representation.

claims.text: The paper contributes a fine-grained catalog from an unchanged canonical filter.
claims.poster_quote: A fine-grained catalog from an unchanged canonical filter
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: a fine-grained catalog of folded views derived from an unchanged canonical filter; and
claims.reason: Section I. The second listed contribution is a fine-grained catalog of folded views derived from an unchanged canonical filter.

claims.text: The paper contributes an evaluation against complete-filter and lossless-compression baselines.
claims.poster_quote: Evaluation against complete-filter and lossless-compression baselines
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: an evaluation against complete-filter and lossless-compression baselines across two datasets and three channel models.
claims.reason: Section I. The third listed contribution is an evaluation against complete-filter and lossless-compression baselines.

claims.text: OR folding splits the bit array and combines positions with bitwise OR.
claims.poster_quote: OR folding splits the bit array and combines positions with bitwise OR
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Conventional one-half folding divides the bit array into two equal regions and combines corresponding positions using bitwise OR.
claims.reason: Section III.B. One-half folding divides the array and combines positions using bitwise OR.

claims.text: The proposed method allows fine-grained retained lengths that need not divide the canonical length, such as 0.95m, 0.90m, or 0.75m.
claims.poster_quote: Unlike one-half folding, we allow fine-grained retained lengths that need not divide the canonical length, such as 0.95m, 0.90m, or 0.75m
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: This work uses the same OR-folding principle but permits fine-grained retained lengths that need not be integer divisors of the canonical filter length. ... Values such as m′ = 0.95m, 0.90m, or 0.75m provide finer-grained communication operating points.
claims.reason: Section III.B. The proposed method permits fine-grained retained lengths such as 0.95m, 0.90m, or 0.75m.

claims.text: Canonical positions sharing the same remainder are merged in OR folding.
claims.poster_quote: canonical positions sharing the same remainder are merged
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Thus, Equation (3) maps every canonical position deterministically into the folded coordinate space and combines positions sharing the same remainder using bitwise OR.
claims.reason: Section III.B. Positions sharing the same remainder are combined using bitwise OR.

claims.text: The sender keeps the canonical filter so views are cached without reinserting elements.
claims.poster_quote: the sender keeps the canonical filter so views are cached without reinserting elements.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The canonical filter remains available at the sender, allowing multiple folded representations to be generated or cached without reinserting the original set elements.
claims.reason: Section III.B. The sender retains the canonical filter, allowing views to be generated or cached without reinserting elements.

claims.text: Queries reuse the same two-stage mapping, so folding preserves no false negatives while raising false positives.
claims.poster_quote: Queries reuse the same two-stage mapping, so folding preserves no false negatives while raising false positives
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: For non-integer folding ratios, membership queries must preserve the same two-stage coordinate mapping used to construct the folded representation. ... Folding therefore preserves the no-false-negative property while potentially increasing false positives, consistent with established OR-folding behavior [2], [7].
claims.reason: Section III.C. Queries use the same two-stage mapping, preserving the no-false-negative property while potentially increasing false positives.

claims.text: The mapping matters because (H_i(x) mod m) mod m' generally differs from H_i(x) mod m'.
claims.poster_quote: the mapping matters because (H_i(x) mod m) mod m’ generally differs from H_i(x) mod m’.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The two-stage mapping is important when m′ is not a divisor of m, because Hi(x) mod m mod m′ is not generally equal to Hi(x) mod m′.
claims.reason: Section III.C. The mapping is important because the two modulo operations are not generally equal.

claims.text: Lower retained ratio r = m'/m merges more positions and increases occupancy.
claims.poster_quote: Lower retained ratio r = m’/m merges more positions and increases occupancy
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Lower values of r merge more canonical positions and increase folded-filter occupancy.
claims.reason: Section III.D. Lower values of r merge more positions and increase occupancy.

claims.text: Because merged positions are not independent, analytic expressions give only intuition and every candidate's FPR is measured directly.
claims.poster_quote: because merged positions are not independent, analytic expressions give only intuition and every candidate’s FPR is measured directly.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Equations (7)–(9) provide intuition rather than an exact prediction because modulo folding can produce unequal preimage sizes when m′ does not divide m, and the merged positions are not strictly independent. The experiments therefore measure the FPR of every candidate representation directly.
claims.reason: Section III.D. Because merged positions are not independent, analytic expressions provide only intuition, and the FPR of every candidate is measured directly.

claims.text: Two phishing datasets, PhiUSIIL and URL-Phish, insert 5,000 malicious URLs and query 50,000 benign URLs.
claims.poster_quote: Two phishing datasets, PhiUSIIL and URL-Phish, insert 5,000 malicious URLs and query 50,000 benign URLs
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The PhiUSIIL [14] and URL-Phish [15] datasets are evaluated using 5,000 malicious URLs for insertion and 50,000 disjoint benign URLs as absent queries.
claims.reason: Section IV.A. The evaluation uses 5,000 malicious URLs for insertion and 50,000 benign URLs as absent queries.

claims.text: In the experimental setup, every positive is a false positive.
claims.poster_quote: every positive is a false positive.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Every positive response to a benign query is therefore a false positive.
claims.reason: Section IV.A. Every positive response to a benign query is a false positive.

claims.text: The sparse canonical filter uses three hash functions for occupancy 0.25 and SHA-256 double hashing.
claims.poster_quote: The sparse canonical filter uses three hash functions for occupancy 0.25 and SHA-256 double hashing
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The sparse canonical filter uses the same m, with its hash count selected for a target occupancy ρ = 0.25: ... Equation (10) produces three hash functions. ... Hash positions use SHA-256 double hashing.
claims.reason: Section IV.B. The sparse filter uses three hash functions for a target occupancy of 0.25 and SHA-256 double hashing.

claims.text: Only views with empirical FPR under 10% enter the catalog.
claims.poster_quote: only views with empirical FPR under 10% enter the catalog.
claims.label: unsupported
claims.reason: Section IV.B states that only representations with an empirical FPR 'no greater than 10%' (which includes exactly 10%) enter the catalog, whereas the claim says 'under 10%' (which excludes 10%).

claims.text: Baselines are uncompressed filters plus gzip, zlib, bzip2 and LZMA.
claims.poster_quote: Baselines are uncompressed filters plus gzip, zlib, bzip2 and LZMA.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The sparse canonical bit array is compared with gzip [17], zlib [18], bzip2 [19], and LZMA [20]. ... Uncompressed classical and sparse filters are also included.
claims.reason: Section IV.C. Baselines include uncompressed filters and the four compression algorithms.

claims.text: Channels evaluated are Five-State Markov, Gilbert-Elliott, and Rayleigh block fading.
claims.poster_quote: Channels: Five-State Markov, Gilbert-Elliott, and Rayleigh block fading.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Using two phishing URL datasets, the framework is evaluated under Five-State Markov Capacity, Gilbert–Elliott burst-error, and Rayleigh block-fading models.
claims.reason: Section Abstract. The evaluated channel models are Five-State Markov, Gilbert-Elliott, and Rayleigh block fading.

claims.text: Fig. 3 shows empirical false-positive rate versus Bloom-filter size reduction, 100(1 - r), where r = m'/m.
claims.poster_quote: Empirical false-positive rate versus Bloom-filter size reduction, 100(1 -r ) , where r = m ’ /m .
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Fig. 3. Empirical false-positive rate versus Bloom-filter size reduction, 100(1 − r), where r = m′/m.
claims.reason: Figure 3 caption. The figure shows empirical false-positive rate versus size reduction.

claims.text: Each curve in Fig. 3 represents one canonical-filter realization for its dataset using the fixed random seed of 42; no averaging across filter-construction seeds was performed.
claims.poster_quote: Each curve represents one canonical-filter realization for its dataset using the fixed random seed of 42; no averaging across filter-construction seeds was performed.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Each curve represents one canonical-filter realization for its dataset using the fixed random seed of 42; no averaging across filter-construction seeds was performed.
claims.reason: Figure 3 caption. Each curve represents one realization using seed 42 without averaging.

claims.text: Selecting the largest FPR-qualified folded view improved communication efficiency and freshness over complete-filter and compression baselines.
claims.poster_quote: Selecting the largest FPR-qualified folded view improved communication efficiency and freshness over complete-filter and compression baselines.
claims.label: unsupported
claims.reason: Section V.B shows that under the Gilbert-Elliott model, adaptive folding does not improve communication efficiency over the strongest compression baseline (140.5 vs 141.8 deliveries per MB).

claims.text: Smaller views trade higher FPR for fresher updates while keeping no false negatives.
claims.poster_quote: Smaller views trade higher FPR for fresher updates while keeping no false negatives.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Smaller views trade increased FPR for fresher updates while preserving the no-false-negative property, complementing rather than replacing lossless compression.
claims.reason: Section VII. Smaller views trade increased FPR for fresher updates while preserving the no-false-negative property.

claims.text: Adaptive folding gives the freshest receiver state under all three channel models.
claims.poster_quote: Adaptive folding gives the freshest receiver state under all three channel models.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Under the more favorable Gilbert–Elliott model, it remains competitive in efficiency while maintaining the freshest receiver state. ... adaptive folding produces the lowest mean age: 0.31 intervals, compared with 0.39 for compression and 0.49 for the classical filter.
claims.reason: Section V.C and Section VII. Adaptive folding achieves the lowest mean age (freshest receiver state) under all three channel models (1.24, 0.31, and 0.40 intervals).

claims.text: Under the Five-State Markov channel model, adaptive folding achieves 1.24 intervals vs 13.5 (compression) and 31.6 (classical).
claims.poster_quote: Five-State Markov: 1.24 intervals vs 13.5 (compression) and 31.6 (classical)
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Under the Five-State Markov Capacity model, adaptive folding reduces mean receiver age to 1.24 intervals, compared with 13.5 for the strongest compression baseline and 31.6 for the classical filter.
claims.reason: Section V.C. Under the Five-State Markov model, adaptive folding achieves 1.24 intervals vs 13.5 (compression) and 31.6 (classical).

claims.text: Under the Gilbert-Elliott channel model, adaptive folding achieves 0.31 intervals vs 0.39 and 0.49 intervals.
claims.poster_quote: Gilbert-Elliott: 0.31 vs 0.39 and 0.49 intervals
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Under the Gilbert–Elliott model, the strongest compression baseline achieves marginally higher communication efficiency, but adaptive folding produces the lowest mean age: 0.31 intervals, compared with 0.39 for compression and 0.49 for the classical filter.
claims.reason: Section V.C. Under the Gilbert-Elliott model, adaptive folding achieves 0.31 intervals vs 0.39 (compression) and 0.49 (classical).

claims.text: Under Rayleigh fading, adaptive folding achieves 0.40 intervals vs 1.02 and 1.72, representing cuts of 61% and 77%.
claims.poster_quote: Rayleigh fading: 0.40 vs 1.02 and 1.72, cuts of 61% and 77%
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Under Rayleigh block fading, adaptive folding achieves a mean age of 0.40, compared with 1.02 for the strongest compression baseline and 1.72 for the classical filter. Receiver age is therefore reduced by approximately 61% relative to compression and 77% relative to the classical filter.
claims.reason: Section V.C. The math is correct: (1.02 - 0.40) / 1.02 = 60.78% (approx 61%) and (1.72 - 0.40) / 1.72 = 76.74% (approx 77%).

claims.text: In Fig. 4, bars show mean successful deliveries per MB and 95% confidence intervals across 20 paired channel traces; higher values indicate better performance.
claims.poster_quote: Bars show mean successful deliveries per MB and 95% confidence intervals across 20 paired channel traces; higher values indicate better performance.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Fig. 4. Communication efficiency under the three channel models. Bars show mean successful deliveries per MB and 95% confidence intervals across 20 paired channel traces; higher values indicate better performance.
claims.reason: Figure 4 caption matches the claim exactly.

claims.text: In Fig. 5, bars show means and 95% confidence intervals across 20 paired channel traces; the vertical axis is logarithmic and lower values indicate fresher receiver state.
claims.poster_quote: Bars show means and 95% confidence intervals across 20 paired channel traces; the vertical axis is logarithmic and lower values indicate fresher receiver state.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Fig. 5. Mean receiver report age under the three channel models. Bars show means and 95% confidence intervals across 20 paired channel traces; the vertical axis is logarithmic and lower values indicate fresher receiver state.
claims.reason: Figure 5 caption matches the claim exactly.

claims.poster_quote: OR-based folding of a 16-bit canonical Bloom filter at r = 0 . 50 and r = 0 . 75 .
claims.label: supported
